# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes managing public finances to reduce national debt as a share of GDP while investing in infrastructure. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The party would reform capital gains tax, increase the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and introduce a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks. Employment reforms include creating a "dependent contractor" status for gig workers, higher minimum wage for zero-hour contracts, and expanded sick pay eligibility.

## Health and Social Care
The manifesto commits to 8,000 additional GPs to enable seven-day appointment guarantees, expanded NHS dentistry access, and mental health hubs in every community. Cancer treatment would have a 62-day guarantee from referral. Social care reforms include introducing free personal care (modeled on Scotland), creating a National Care Agency, establishing a Royal College of Care Workers, and increasing Carer's Allowance with expanded eligibility.

## Education
Proposals include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment would include extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds.

## Housing and Planning
The party targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through ten new garden cities and planning reforms. Measures include banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leasehold, and allowing councils to end Right to Buy locally.

## Environment and Energy
Climate targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home insulation programme would prioritise low-income households. Water companies would become public benefit companies with sewage discharge bans. The manifesto proposes doubling protected areas, woodland cover, and species abundance by 2050.

## Transport
Proposals include freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, restoring the 2030 zero-emission vehicle mandate, expanding EV charging infrastructure, and giving local authorities powers to franchise bus services.

## Immigration and Asylum
The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish a three-month asylum processing standard, allow asylum seekers to work after three months, and create safe legal routes for refugees. Work visa policy would transfer to relevant departments with sector-specific approaches.

## Political Reform
Constitutional changes include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, scrapping voter ID requirements, capping political donations, and reforming the House of Lords. The Ministerial Code would be enshrined in law.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP with Army cuts reversed. The party supports NATO, maintaining nuclear deterrent, and continued Ukraine support. International development would return to 0.7% of national income. On Europe, a four-stage roadmap aims to rebuild relations, culminating in Single Market membership, with EU membership as a longer-term objective.
